summary.title: Build Your Own Redis: Introduction [0/4]
summary.one_liner: An overview of a series that builds a toy Redis clone in Ruby, handling PING, ECHO, SET and GET over the Redis protocol.
takeaways: Redis is a data store supporting data structures like strings, hashes, lists and sets, and clients talk to it over TCP using the Redis Protocol.
The series builds a toy Redis server in Ruby that responds to PING, ECHO, SET and GET.
A TCP server is spawned that binds to a port and accepts client connections.
An event loop lets one thread serve multiple clients, mirroring the official Redis design.
The implementation speaks the Redis protocol, so the official redis-cli can talk to it.
summary.summary: This is the introductory article of a four-part (plus in-progress) series that builds a toy Redis clone in Ruby. It explains briefly what Redis is and shows a sample redis-cli session with PING, SET and GET. The article then outlines the stages: a barebones TCP server, PING/PONG replies using the Redis protocol, concurrent clients via an event loop, ECHO with RESP parsing, and SET/GET with state. The page notes that the SET & GET part is still in progress.
